1.title: Hop, Skip, Jump!
1.topic: hopping, skipping, jumping and spinning in gym class, then resting on the mat (school, exercise, play)
sounds: 입을 동그랗고 크게 벌려 짧게 '아': hop '합', top '탑'.
'이'를 짧고 힘 빼서: skip '스킵', sit '씻'. 길게 '이-' 하지 않아요.
s와 다음 소리를 붙여 한 번에: 'sk', 'sp', 'st'. '스'를 따로 크게 내지 않아요.
1.expression: Bounce your voice on “Hop, hop, hop!” and “Jump, jump, jump!”, ask “Can you hop and spin?” with your voice going up, answer a proud “Yes, I can!”, and finish slow and happy: “That was fun!”

2.title: Oops, Blue Paint!
2.topic: a boy spills blue paint on his boat picture in art class and turns the mess into an ocean (school, art, mistakes, feelings)
sounds: ch, p, k 뒤는 짧은 t: tipped '팁트', looked '룩트'.
l, n 뒤는 약한 d: spilled '스필드', sailed '세일드'.
2.expression: Start calm and happy while Owen paints, drop your voice on a surprised “oops!”, sound upset on “My picture is ruined!”, give Ms. Kim a kind, thinking voice, get excited on “It can be the sea!”, and end proud and bright on the blue ocean.

3.title: What Am I? Animal Riddles
3.topic: three animal riddles with clues about a giraffe, a sloth and a hummingbird (animals, science, guessing game)
lines: I have a *very* *long* *neck* | and *spots* *all* over my *body*.
I *eat* *leaves* from the *tops* of *tall* *trees*. | *What* am I? ↘
I'm a *giraffe*! ↘ | My *tongue* is *dark* *purple* | and *almost* as *long* as your *arm*.
I *hang* from *branches* | and *sleep* for *many* *hours* a *day*. | *What* am I? ↘
I'm a *sloth*! ↘ | I'm *so* *slow* | that *tiny* *green* *plants* can *grow* on my *fur*.
My *wings* *flap* so *fast* | that they make a *humming* *sound*. | *What* am I? ↘
*Now* it's *your* *turn*. | Can *you* make a *riddle* | about your *favorite* *animal*? ↗
sounds: giraffe는 뒤 음절 'RAFFE'에 힘! 나머지는 첫 음절을 크게 읽어요: 'RAIN-포레스트'.
혀끝을 윗니 아래로 살짝 내밀고 바람을 내보내요. sloth는 '슬로스'가 아니라 끝에 혀를 물어 'θ'.
tongue의 -ue는 소리 없음 '텅', guess의 u도 소리 없음 '게스'.
3.expression: Read like a quiz-show host: lively on “Listen to my clues,” clear and slow on each clue so friends can think, drop your voice on every “What am I?”, then reveal each answer with a big, happy “I'm a giraffe!” Make the sloth part sleepy and slow, the hummingbird part quick and light, and ask the last question with a friendly, rising voice.
practice: almost as long as your arm

4.title: The Case of the Vanishing Puddle
4.topic: a girl detective investigates why a driveway puddle disappeared and Grandma explains evaporation and the water cycle (science, weather, family, mystery)
lines: On *Saturday* *morning*, | a *huge* *puddle* *sat* | in the *middle* of our *driveway*.
But by *three* o'*clock*, | the puddle had *shrunk* | to the *size* of a *pizza*.
*Next*, I *looked* for a *drain* *nearby*, | but the driveway was *flat* and *solid*.
“The *sun* was the *thief*,” | she said with a *wink*.
Grandma *pointed* at the *clouds*. | “*Someday* it will *fall* *again* | as *rain*.” ↘
I *wrote* in my *notebook*: | *Case* *closed*. | The puddle is *just* on *vacation*! ↘
sounds: 강세 위치가 달라요! detective는 둘째 'TEC', invisible은 'VIS', evaporation은 '-RA-'를 크고 길게.
끝의 -dle은 '들'처럼 혀끝을 윗잇몸에 붙인 채 끝내요: puddle '퍼들', middle '미들'.
혀끝을 이 사이에 살짝: three는 '쓰리'가 아니라 'θree', thief도 'θief'.
4.expression: Tell it like a detective story: calm and ordinary at the start, puzzled as the puddle shrinks, surprised on “it had vanished completely!”, loud and silly in Eli's voice, serious and step-by-step for First, Next and Finally, slow and wise in Grandma's voice, worried on Eli's rising question, and proud and funny on “Case closed.”
practice: The puddle is just on vacation!
